You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hotspot Sniper｜2026.07.15

TEXT:
Main Theme: AI Storage and Chip Collaboration Catalyze Rebound｜SK Hynix Surge · NVIDIA Data Center · Apple On-Device AI
1. SK Hynix ADR Surges to New High
SK Hynix US ADR ( SKHY .US) rose over 27% to $193.92, hitting a new listing high with a market cap of $1.36 trillion, trading at a premium of over 45% to its Korean shares. The direct catalyst was a bullish report from top research firm SemiAnalysis titled “Be Greedy When Others Are Fearful.” SK Hynix ADR options officially began trading on US options exchanges on Tuesday, offering new tools for investors in the global derivatives market. Piper Sandler options head Daniel Kirsch expects investors to mainly position for short-term upside this week. As of press time , the Korean shares were up over 10% in early trading.
🎯 Beneficiaries: SKHY; Key Catalyst: Top-tier bullish report + options listing attracting derivatives capital, strong AI memory demand.
2. NVIDIA Plans Collaboration with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries on AI Data Centers
According to Nikkei, NVIDIA is considering a partnership with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (7011.JP) to provide cooling systems and energy management equipment for AI data centers. NVIDIA refers to next-gen AI data centers as “AI Factories” and plans to build them with global partners. In Japan and Korea, SK Group is already collaborating with NVIDIA on an AI factory slated for 2028-2029. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries produces air conditioning, high-efficiency cooling, emergency power equipment, and integrated energy management systems for data centers.
🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA; Key Catalyst: Landing of data center cooling and power solutions, continued expansion of AI infrastructure demand.
3. Apple Evaluates On-Device AI Model Compression
Apple is in early discussions with Silicon Valley startup PrismML on AI model compression technology that claims to run 27B-parameter large models directly on iPhone, strengthening privacy advantages and paving the way for Siri upgrades. The news came the day after the iOS 27 public beta launch — Apple’s first broad public test following major Siri revisions to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic assistants. Keeping more AI compute on-device means lower latency, reduced cloud costs, and offline functionality, aligning with Apple’s core privacy positioning.
🎯 Beneficiaries: AAPL ; Key Catalyst: On-device AI validation advancing, Siri overhaul in testing window.
4. IBM Issues Earnings Warning, Sparking Software Sector Concerns
IBM issued an unexpected Q2 earnings warning, triggering its largest single-day stock drop on record. Goldman Sachs warned that the shift in corporate IT budgets toward AI infrastructure could confirm a “software bear market,” with broad downward pressure on software and services.
🎯 Beneficiaries: IBM; Key Catalyst: Validation of enterprise IT budget shift to AI infrastructure, watch for downside pressure on software/services.
5. Lucid Denies Privatization or Bankruptcy Rumors US EV maker
Lucid Group ( LCID .US) denied reports of considering privatization or Chapter 11 bankruptcy, calling them “completely false.” The stock plunged over 50% intraday (largest single-day drop since listing) but narrowed to a 16% loss after the denial. Lucid stated it has sufficient liquidity to support operations well into next year, no special committee was formed, and advisor AlixPartners is helping improve operational efficiency rather than preparing for bankruptcy. 🎯 Beneficiaries: LCID; Key Catalyst: Rumor clarification supporting valuation recovery, monitor liquidity and execution improvements.
Trading Tips: AI memory (SKHY) and data center collaborations (NVDA) drive hotspot rebounds, while Apple on-device AI and IBM warning create divergence in tech sectors. Focus on AI infrastructure capital flows and options activity; manage positions cautiously amid volatility. US stocks have seen heightened volatility recently. The above is for information reference only and does not constitute investment advice.
